sections.label: Parcel delivery volume growth
sections.summary: Parcel deliveries are part of everyday life and domestic e-commerce parcel volume is projected to grow at 16% annually to 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: While we might receive fewer letters now, more of us are shopping online and parcel deliveries have become part of everyday life The volume of parcel delivery is expected to intensify given that domestic e-commerce parcel volume growth in Singapore is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 16% from now to 2025.

sections.label: Updating PSA for last mile
sections.summary: The PSA is to be updated for last mile delivery, as about 7% of deliveries are unsuccessful, inconveniencing consumers and reducing DSP productivity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: It is thus timely to update the PSA in response to the evolving landscape of last mile delivery amidst increasing digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: However, based on industry estimates, about 7% of deliveries are unsuccessful, causing inconvenience to consumers and reducing the productivity of delivery service providers, or DSPs.

sections.label: 1,000 parcel lockers rollout
sections.summary: The Ministry announced 1,000 parcel lockers will be rolled out in HDB estates, MRT stations, bus interchanges and Community Centres and Clubs by year end.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: To enhance DSPs' productivity and efficiency of Singapore's urban logistics sector, my Ministry previously announced that 1,000 parcel lockers will be rolled out in HDB estates, MRT stations, bus interchanges and Community Centres and Clubs by the end of this year.

sections.label: Pick Network as public infrastructure
sections.summary: Pick Network Pte Ltd was set up as a fully owned IMDA subsidiary to establish, install, operate and maintain the Network as public infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: To best serve the interest of consumers and the industry and to avoid conferring an unfair competitive advantage upon any single player, Pick Network Pte Ltd, or Pick, was set up as a fully owned subsidiary of IMDA to establish, install, operate and maintain the Network as public infrastructure.

sections.label: IMDA network operator powers
sections.summary: New section 23C empowers IMDA to appoint a network operator, and sections 23H to 23K impose obligations on owners and developers of specified premises.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The new section 23C empowers IMDA to appoint a network operator to carry out the duties mentioned in section 23B, subject to any conditions specified by IMDA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The new sections 23H to 23K will introduce obligations on owners and developers of buildings or land designated as specified premises to provide suitable space or facilities and access thereto for the installation or maintenance of the Network.

sections.label: Offences and enforcement powers
sections.summary: The Bill introduces offences relating to the Network and converse enforcement powers, largely similar to those for postal services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: To address these concerns, the Bill introduces offences relating to the Network and converse enforcement powers in relation to these offences, which are largely similar to those in place for postal services.

sections.label: Wholesale access to parcel lockers
sections.summary: New section 7A lets licensing terms require a PPL to offer DSPs wholesale access for delivering small packets and parcels that fit letterboxes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Under the new section 7A, a PPL can be required via licensing terms and conditions to offer wholesale access to DSPs for the delivery of small packets and parcels which can fit into letterboxes, in addition to its existing provision of wholesale access for the delivery of letters.

sections.label: Offence for failing Minister directions
sections.summary: Clause 17 amends section 45 to make non-compliance with Ministerial directions an offence, with fines of up to $1 million and $100,000 per day.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Clause 17 amends section 45 to make it an offence for postal licensees to fail to comply with directions given by the Minister.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The maximum fine for such an offence is $1 million, and a maximum further fine of $100,000 for each day or part of a day should the offence continue after conviction.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The amendments will provide the industry and consumers with the confidence to use the Network's lockers, and create an improved experience for DSPs and consumers alike.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Stakeholders will gain clarity on requirements for letterbox infrastructure, and the urban logistics sector will also stand to gain from access to letterboxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The amendments are a timely response to the evolving postal landscape due to the growth in e-commerce deliveries and accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: Expanding IMDA privilege to parcel lockers
sections.summary: The Bill expands IMDA's exclusive privilege to cover installation and ownership of the Public Parcel Locker Network, with an appointed operator and specified locations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Perhaps the postal authority should re-look at such scenarios and establish better mechanisms for dispute resolution or mandate the way transactions are carried out so that buyers are not left with little or time-consuming recourse as many of these items may be of small or lower value purchases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: It is against this backdrop that I applaud this Bill which seeks to expand the scope of IMDA's exclusive privilege to include the installation and ownership of the Public Parcel Locker Network, hereinafter referred to as the "Network".

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: There will also be powers for IMDA to appoint an operator for the installation, operation and maintenance of the Network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I understand that the Network will be implemented in certain areas, namely, HDB estates, bus interchanges, train stations and/or Community Clubs managed by the People's Association.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The Network will cater to the growing demand of e-commerce purchases, while simultaneously alleviating the problem of failed doorstep deliveries.

sections.label: Questions on private estates and seniors
sections.summary: The member asks whether the initiative will extend to private estates and condominiums and how MCI and IMDA will support residents, especially senior citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: While residents living in HDB estates will no doubt stand to benefit from this initiative, are there plans to extend the same to those living in private estates and condominiums?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Additionally, how will MCI and IMDA provide the necessary support to residents, in particular, senior citizens to facilitate such transition and especially when the packages may be heavy and the intent for home delivery is to minimise the challenges of carrying the heavy load?

sections.label: Training and welfare of delivery workers
sections.summary: NTUC commits to working with companies through Company Training Committees to train postmen and last mile delivery workers, and urges raising their wages and welfare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: On NTUC's end, we are committed to working with companies, through the development of Company Training Committees, to ensure that our postmen and last mile delivery workers are adequately trained to perform their delivery roles once the Network is established.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I submit that regulators and employers of these postal and last mile delivery workers to raise their wages, welfare, and work prospects as they are essential workers in the next normal of a low touch digitalised economy.

sections.label: Clarity on Pick Network's role
sections.summary: The member welcomes the Network's creation but seeks more clarity on the role of Pick Network Pte Ltd in the existing ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While I welcome the creation of the Network, I would like to more clarity on the role of Pick Network Pte Ltd, in the existing ecosystem.

sections.label: IMDA private sector parcel lockers
sections.summary: The passage asks why IMDA did not contract private sector players to provide more public parcel lockers near housing estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What was the reason why IMDA did not contract these private sector players to provide more public parcel lockers near housing estates?

sections.label: Public tender for locker network
sections.summary: The passage asks whether there was a public tender for the deployment and operation of a public locker network that Pick eventually won.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Was there a public tender for the deployment and operation of a public locker network, which Pick eventually won?

sections.label: IMDA spending on Pick operations
sections.summary: The passage asks how much IMDA has spent and will budget yearly to subsidise Pick's operations if there was no tender.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If not, how much has IMDA spend and how much will it be budgeting every year to subsidise their operations of Pick?

sections.label: Hazardous materials in lockers
sections.summary: The passage states MRT stations and community centres were selected for lockers and raises concern about hazardous materials deposited there.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In order to increase the accessibility of these lockers, MRT stations and community centres have been selected as two of the main locations where lockers will be installed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As these are places where traffic is high, my concern is that hazardous materials which might cause harm and danger to commuters could be deposited there.

sections.label: Elderly parcel locker accessibility
sections.summary: The passage says senior citizens' needs should be considered from the design stage and a visible large-font step-by-step guide placed at locker stations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: With our rapidly ageing population, it is important to ensure that from the design stage, consideration of the needs of senior citizens is taken into account so that they can benefit from the set-up of these parcel lockers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I realise that many elderly may not know how to use these parcel lockers to retrieve their delivered parcels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Thus, it is important that a step-by-step guide in large fonts be placed at the parcel locker station area which is very visible and at eye level so that they can read the guide while unlocking the lockers.

sections.label: Online sale and e-commerce growth
sections.summary: The passage states 16,000 items were sold per minute in the first 11 minutes and cites JPMorgan on e-commerce growth from 2017 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Specifically, in the first 11 minutes of the online sale, 16,000 items were sold every minute amounting to a total of 176,000 items purchased by Singaporeans in the first few opening minutes of the sale.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The 2020 E-commerce Payments Trends Report for Singapore by JPMorgan estimated that the value of business to consumer e-commerce has grown from US$4.8 billion to US$6.1 billion, or a US$1.3 billion rise, between 2017 and 2019.

sections.label: Nationwide parcel locker network framework
sections.summary: The Postal Services (Amendment) Bill establishes a framework to build and operate a nationwide parcel locker network to help domestic last mile delivery at scale.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Postal Services (Amendment) Bill establishes a framework to build and operate a nationwide parcel locker network, or what I will call NPLN for short, to help domestic last mile delivery at scale.

sections.label: Hack of Moscow package lockers
sections.summary: A hack on a service provider maintaining package lockers across Moscow and Saint Petersburg unlocked more than 2,700 lockers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In December last year, a hack on a service provider that maintained a network of package lockers across Moscow and Saint Petersburg resulted in more than 2,700 lockers being unlocked.

sections.label: Missed deliveries and e-commerce growth
sections.summary: Customers miss delivery windows and worry about package safety, while growing e-commerce volumes increase the complexity, cost and carbon emission of urban logistics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, customers often miss the delivery window, then worry that their packages are not safe.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And, with the increasing volume of e-commerce transactions which is projected to reach US$2.9 billion in 2021 according to Statisca, the urban logistics of getting the packages to the intended recipients is going to grow in complexity and, very likely, so in cost and carbon emission.

sections.label: IMDA pilots and PICK locker installation
sections.summary: IMDA pilots with e-commerce and logistics players in two HDB estates showed benefits, and PICK will install locker networks in HDB estates, community centres and MRT stations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And the good part is that IMDA has implemented pilots in collaboration with e-commerce and logistics industry players in two HDB estates and the study has shown benefits for both consumers and industry players and the potential of a sustainable delivery eco-system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is, in my opinion, an excellent example of public infrastructure that will ensure that all Singaporeans will be served as IMDA’s subsidiary, PICK, will install the locker networks in HDB estates, community centres and MRT stations and these will complement the commercial locker networks in commercial malls and office buildings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Three, there will be wholesale access to SingPost letter box infrastructure for non-letters, small parcels, under regulated terms and conditions.

sections.label: Supporting SME delivery operators
sections.summary: The question asks how IMDA will ensure PICK supports smaller SME delivery operators to embrace digitalisation, improve productivity and reduce costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Better user experience will increase the value consumers will be willing to pay for the service.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, my question is: how will IMDA ensure that PICK supports the smaller SME delivery operators to embrace digitalisation and improve productivity and, thereby, reduce costs ?

sections.label: Locker system delivery estimates
sections.summary: The development is timely given e-commerce growth and doorstep deliveries, and the locker system was estimated to enable drivers to make up to four times more deliveries per hour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is a timely development in view of the exponential growth in e-commerce and the ever-increasing number of doorstep deliveries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It was estimated that the locker system will enable delivery drivers to make up to four times more deliveries per hour.

sections.label: Parcel lockers in HDB estates
sections.summary: Parcel lockers are mostly in commercial areas, leaving residential areas under-served, and the speaker welcomes 800 open access locker stations in HDB estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Presently, parcel lockers are mostly located in commercial areas and our residential areas are under-served since the private sector does not perceive it profitable to install lockers in housing estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I welcome the plan to install 800 open access parcel locker stations in our HDB estates.

sections.label: Cold storage parcel lockers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry would consider installing cold storage parcel lockers, such as those set up in Finland.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: (In English): Would the Ministry also consider installing cold storage parcel lockers, such as those set up in Finland?

sections.label: Library books via locker network
sections.summary: The speaker asks if the National Library Board could allow books to be sent and returned via the locker network for disadvantaged children, noting mail volume changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In addition, can the National Library Board consider allowing its books to be sent and returned via this locker network so that disadvantaged children can also have easy access to books?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the last decade, the mail volume of letters has declined by almost 30%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: At the same time, the volume of non-letters, such as small packages and parcels, has increased – largely driven by the proliferation of online shopping platforms and changing consumption patterns.

sections.label: National parcel locker network framework
sections.summary: A new framework is needed for changing communications and last-mile delivery, and Postal Services Act amendments let IMDA deploy a standardised national parcel locker network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A new framework needs to be set up to enable our postal service provider to meet changing patterns of communications and to close the last-mile delivery gap for small packages and parcels for consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am thus heartened to know that the amendments to the Postal Services Act have made provisions for IMDA to deploy a standardised national network of parcel lockers via a wholly-owned subsidiary or through an appointed vendor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This fragmentation would make it challenging for merchants to adopt a standardised approach to last-mile delivery and for consumers to have a reliable method to receive their parcels when they shop from different online merchants that might perhaps use different locker platforms, depending on their tie-ups and partnerships with those providers and vendors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Thus, I believe that market consolidation in the parcel locker service will help to minimise current market disamenities, such as differing operational standards, non-systematic deployment of lockers and deployment of competing lockers in already congested public spaces.

sections.label: Sufficiency of lockers locally
sections.summary: For the initiative to work, the Government needs to ensure the sufficiency of the lockers at the local level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For this initiative to work, the Government needs to ensure the sufficiency of the lockers, at the local level.

sections.label: Door-step delivery and logistics savings
sections.summary: Businesses offering essential goods should continue door-step delivery, and the speaker asks how much logistics service providers can expect to save using the network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As such, businesses, particularly those offering essential goods and services, should continue to offer door-step delivery as an option and, hopefully, not at an unreasonable premium.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Government share how much can logistics service providers expect to save, if they utilise this network?

sections.label: Delivery jobs affected by lockers
sections.summary: The question asks how many delivery jobs will be affected by the locker initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Government share how many delivery jobs will be affected as a result of the locker initiative?

sections.label: Nationwide parcel locker network standards
sections.summary: Pick Network Pte Ltd provides a nationwide parcel locker network with standards and guidelines to protect customers and businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With the provision of a nationwide parcel locker network via Pick Network Pte Ltd, we are able to provide standards and guidelines in order to protect customers and businesses.

sections.label: Locker network and last mile operators
sections.summary: A nationwide parcel locker network open to last mile delivery operators would promote more effective use of valuable space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Provision of a nationwide parcel locker network and allowing access to these assets to last mile delivery operators would help promote more effective use of valuable space.

sections.label: Failed doorstep delivery rate
sections.summary: Current businesses and customers face a 7% failed delivery rate at doorstep, and locker access can raise successful delivery rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Current businesses and customers face a 7% failed delivery rate at doorstep.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Access to network of lockers will enable last mile delivery providers to increase their successful delivery rate.

sections.label: Customers no longer wait at home
sections.summary: Customers are better off because they no longer have to remain at home anticipating a delivery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Customers are better off as they no longer have to remain at home in anticipation of a delivery.

sections.label: Fraudulent claims affect delivery riders
sections.summary: For delivery riders earning less than $5 per successful delivery, fraudulent claims can affect their income and cause loss of income for days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For delivery riders earning less than $5 per successful delivery, fraudulent claims can affect their income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Fraudulent claims may cause delivery riders to lose their entire income for a few days.

sections.label: Postal Service Act amendments and parcel lockers
sections.summary: The amendments to the Postal Service Act aim to keep the postal service relevant, with automated parcel machines offering convenient pickup for those who prefer it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The amendments to the Postal Service Act will ensure the continued relevance of our postal service to future generations of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While such lockers, also known as automated parcel machines, or APMs, may not be able to replace the role of couriers who compete by delivering right to the doorstep, they offer a convenient service to those who prefer to pick up their parcels at time slots convenient to them.

sections.label: PUDOs, delivery volumes and worker upskilling
sections.summary: PUDOs need no installation, can be set up flexibly and help cope with peak delivery volumes, and the speaker asks about plans to train workers and use technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: PUDOs, which require no installation, can be set up more flexibly and can help to cope with increased delivery volumes during peak hours when the demand for APMs is high and they get filled up quickly, such as during the Christmas season.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also hope that the Ministry will work with condominiums and private estates to enhance the out of home delivery options for them, through a combination of APM and PUDO locations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What are the plans to train and upskill this group of essential workers, and how are we supporting them by tapping on technology, such as robotic delivery assistants?

sections.label: SingPost fine for delivery standards
sections.summary: In 2019, SingPost was fined a record $400,000 for failing to meet delivery standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2019, SingPost was hit with a record $400,000 fine for failing to meet delivery standards.

sections.label: IMDA parcel locker stations rollout
sections.summary: Ahead of this Bill, IMDA announced it will roll out 1,000 parcel locker stations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Ahead of this Bill, IMDA announced that it will roll out 1,000 parcel locker stations.

sections.label: Regulated Wholesale Access for SingPost
sections.summary: The proposed amendments will implement Regulated Wholesale Access, requiring SingPost to deliver small packages for other delivery service providers into letter boxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, the proposed amendments will implement Regulated Wholesale Access which means that SingPost will be required to deliver small packages for other delivery service providers into letter boxes.

sections.label: Parcel trackability throughout delivery process
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry or IMDA has looked into how parcel trackability can be maintained throughout the delivery process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify whether the Ministry or IMDA has looked into how the trackability of parcels can be maintained throughout the delivery process?

sections.label: Network parcel delivery convenience
sections.summary: The speaker said the Network is an efficient solution offering greater convenience and more parcel delivery options beyond doorstep delivery.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In my opening speech, I spoke about how the Network is an efficient solution that provides greater convenience and more options for parcel deliveries beyond doorstep delivery.

sections.label: Residents would use Pick lockers
sections.summary: Ninety-six percent of residents said they would use Pick's lockers for 24/7 self-collection and safe access to deliveries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Ninety-six percent of residents indicated that they would use Pick's lockers due to reasons such as the convenience of 24/7 self-collection and the confidence of being able to access their deliveries safely rather than having their parcels being left at their doorstep unattended.

sections.label: DSPs hand parcels to SingPost
sections.summary: Other DSPs can already hand parcels to SingPost for tracked letterbox delivery on commercial terms, so tracking is unaffected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Please allow me to clarify that today, other DSPs are already able to hand over their packets and parcels to SingPost for delivery into letterboxes on commercially negotiated terms on a tracked basis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Hence, consumers' ability to track the delivery of their packets and parcels to letterboxes will not be affected by this amendment.

sections.label: Parcel locker security guidelines
sections.summary: IMDA is working with MHA and SCDF to develop security guidelines and requirements for locker design and parcel handling workflows.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Similarly, we will also guard against mischief and tampering in the parcel locker setting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We are working closely with MHA and SCDF to develop security guidelines and requirements to ensure that the locker design and parcel handling workflows meet required safety and security standards.

sections.label: IMDA notices and prohibited items
sections.summary: IMDA can issue written notices to Pick on security compliance, and section 39J makes placing prohibited items in lockers an offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: IMDA will be empowered to issue written notices to Pick in relation to Pick's compliance with security requirements and guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Relatedly, the new section 39J makes it an offence for a person to place prohibited items in the Network's parcel lockers.

sections.label: CCTV at Pick locker stations
sections.summary: Each Pick locker station will have two CCTV cameras with round-the-clock surveillance to aid theft investigations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Mr Patrick Tay will be glad to know that each Pick locker station will include two CCTV cameras with round-the-clock video surveillance, which will aid potential investigations into any incidents of theft.

sections.label: Technical Reference 76 e-commerce retailers
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore and the Singapore Standards Council launched Technical Reference 76, which outlines e-commerce retailers' responsibility for lost or damaged items during delivery.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In this regard, Enterprise Singapore and the Singapore Standards Council have launched the Technical Reference 76 (TR 76), which outlines e-commerce retailers' responsibility among others on the handling of lost or damaged items during delivery to protect consumers' interests.

sections.label: Locker Alliance pilot delivery efficiency
sections.summary: Based on the Locker Alliance pilot from 2018, participating DSPs reported a four-fold increase in delivery efficiency with 70 parcel locker stations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Based on the Locker Alliance pilot which started in 2018, participating DSPs reported a four-fold increase in delivery efficiency with just 70 parcel locker stations, established in two HDB towns and eight MRT stations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: With a nationwide Network of 1,000 parcel lockers stations, the potential productivity gains for the industry will be significant.

sections.label: Government-operated parcel locker Network
sections.summary: IMDA formed a subsidiary, Pick, to operate a Government-run parcel locker Network, allowing IMDA to manage placements and timelines while ensuring reasonable prices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We listened to the voices from the industry and we very seriously considered having a neutral operator that industry stakeholders will have confidence in, in providing that open access to everyone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We believe that these twin objectives that I have outlined would be best served by a Network operated by the Government – in this case, it would be IMDA – and to give effect to this intention, IMDA formed a subsidiary, Pick.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Having Pick, an IMDA subsidiary, operate the Network will allow IMDA to directly manage locker placements and deployment timelines while ensuring prices are reasonable and affordable.

sections.label: Pick's exclusive privileges confined
sections.summary: Pick's exclusive privileges are confined to providing parcel lockers at specified premises only.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Pick's exclusive privileges are confined to the provision of parcel lockers at specified premises only.

sections.label: Pick's IMDA resilience security requirements
sections.summary: Pick must comply with IMDA requirements for Network resilience and security, including vulnerability testing by independent cybersecurity experts before lockers are available.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Pick will have to comply with requirements set out by IMDA to ensure the resilience and security of the Network before, during and after the deployment of the Network.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: For example, the software component will be subject to vulnerability testing by independent cybersecurity experts, before the parcel lockers are available for use.

sections.label: Bill amendments postal landscape shifts
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments for nationwide locker deployment, letterbox infrastructure and postal services regulation will ready Singapore for digital shifts in its postal landscape.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Taken together, the amendments in this Bill to effect nationwide deployment of lockers in tandem with the changes pertaining to letterbox infrastructure and regulation of postal services, will ready us for the digital and technological shifts in our postal landscape.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: They will enable us to embrace the global search in e-commerce while putting us in good stead to cope with manpower constraints in the sector with a more skilled and better-equipped postal workforce ready to face the challenges of the digital age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: These will ultimately benefit consumers and the industry alike.

sections.label: Pick lockers funding and launch
sections.summary: Pick lockers are expected to go live later this month, and IMDA does not intend long-term subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: In the long term, will Pick be profit-oriented, or will it be subsidised by IMDA?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The lockers in fact will be going live, we hope, later this month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: However, what I can share is that we do intend for it to become a well-functioning part of the eco-system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We do believe that there are certain gaps in the market that do need to be plugged so that the previous inefficiencies that we have described, will then be eliminated but we do not intend for this to be done at the expense of long-term subsidies.
